full_judgment: 3. The contrary case of the defendant in short is thus that the superior landlord of the plaintiffs' predecessors was MT Brown Estate under Court of Wards and the land of CS Khatian No. 145 was auction purchased by the superior landlord. Beside this the land of CS Khatian No. 142 was also sold in a certificate case and was purchased by the superior landlord. The Court of Wards took possession of the land through court against which the predecessor of the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 139 of 1945 challenging the auction sale which was dismissed for default. Subsequently, the Court of Wards granted settlement in favour of one Jonab Ali by granting 'dakhilas' and those properties have been recorded in the name of the defendants during Revisional Settlement and State Acquisition operation. The land of Petty Settlement Khatian No. 108 was purchased by the government and the government resettled the same in part to the defendants and in part to the plaintiffs. Apart from this, the land of PS Khatian No. 140/2 was auction purchased by government for arrear of rent and the government leased out the same to the predecessor of the defendant Jonab Ali and one Nawab Ali Mia. The further case of the defendants is such that the SA Khatian has been correctly prepared in their names and they had been owning and possessing the suit land after construction of homestead and they have donated 0.30 acres of land in favour of the government for establishment of a 'Hat'.
